name: UniFi Protect
author: Jankees van Woezik
description: UniFi Protect cameras: one icon in the bar, the pictures in a panel

barWidget.description: UniFi Protect cameras: one icon in the bar, the pictures in a panel

schema.label: Gateway
schema.description: Address of the console running Protect: a UDM, a Cloud Key, or whatever else answers on your network. An IP address or a hostname, without the scheme.

schema.label: Cameras that may interrupt you
schema.description: Camera names, comma separated, exactly as Protect spells them. Empty means every camera. This gates the bar icon and the archive both: the camera aimed at your own desk reports motion all day, and an icon that is always lit is an icon you stop reading.

schema.label: Raise a notification on motion
schema.description: A desktop notification with the frame in it, so motion reaches you when the bar is not where you are looking.

schema.label: Panel width
schema.description: In the shell's spacing units. The live view is this wide and everything else is measured off it, so this one number sizes the whole panel. Anything wider than the screen is trimmed to fit.

schema.label: Keep the icon lit for
schema.description: Milliseconds. Protect sends a start and, later, an end; this is the floor under a burst that ends immediately, so a moment of movement is still there when you look up.

schema.label: Snapshot interval
schema.description: Milliseconds between stills for the selected camera while the video stream is connecting or has dropped out. Once the stream plays, this stops.

schema.label: Leave a camera alone for
schema.description: Milliseconds after filing a frame in which the same camera files nothing more. Protect can report a dozen starts while one person walks past the door.

schema.label: Frames kept per camera
schema.description: The archive under the panel. Frames are stored around 960px wide, so sixty of them is a few megabytes and covers a busy day.

schema.label: RTSP port
schema.description: Protect hands out an encrypted rtsps:// URL that Qt cannot be told to trust, so the live view reads the same stream off the plain RTSP port instead. 7447 unless you have moved it.

schema.label: Where a click on the picture goes
schema.description: Protect's detection browser, filtered to the camera you clicked. {host} is the gateway above and {camera} the camera id. A setting rather than a constant, because Protect is a single-page app: this route was read off the address bar and a UniFi update is free to move it.
